name: Tiefo-D
catalog_citation: Heath, Jeffrey & Aminata Ouattara. 2021. A Grammar of Tiefo-D of Daramandugu (Niger-Congo language, Burkina Faso). Language Description Heritage Library; Zenodo record 4715103 (BW PDF).
catalog_locator: sec. 3.6 Tones, p.79; sec. 3.5 Cliticization, p.75; sketch sec. 2.1.2 Tones and prosody, p.7
catalog_quote: 3.6 Tones: There are three tone levels, H[igh], M[id], and L[ow]. None of these can be reduced to an allophone of one of the others. There is no evidence in favor of an accentual interpretation of tones. Contour tones on individual syllables, other than those due to vv-Contraction across boundaries. are <HL> and <LH>. ... 3.5 Cliticization: Tiefo-D belongs to the set of languages that have a) fixed word order, b) numerous grammatical particles, and c) no stress or accent shifts due to addition of a morpheme. In such languages, it can be difficult to distinguish cliticization from simple linear juxtaposition. ... 2.1.2 Tones and prosody: Tiefo-D has three tone levels, high, mid, and low, like several other languages of SW Burkina.

new_statements.locator: §3.6 Tones, p. 79 (PDF p. 102); §3.5 Cliticization, p. 75 (PDF p. 98); also §2.1.2 Tones and prosody, pp. 7-8, and §3.7 Intonation, pp. 102-103
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog holds Tiefo-D with an empty rule and no existing stress statements. This grammar fills that gap: it establishes the language as a three-tone language and explicitly denies an accentual interpretation of the tones and any morpheme-induced stress/accent shift, so the catalog entry should be recorded as tonal, no word-stress rule stated, rather than left blank.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tiefo-D is a three-level tone language (H, M, L; lexical contrasts on nouns, e.g. dɛ́ 'body' / dɛ̄ 'elder sibling' / dɛ̀ 'field'; contours HL and LH on single syllables; verbs level-toned with Pfv one notch below base/Ipfv). The grammar has no stress section; its only statements about stress/accent are negative: tones are not reducible to an accentual (pitch accent) system, and adding a morpheme never triggers a stress or accent shift. No word-stress placement is given; the prosody chapter covers tone sandhi (M#H -> L#H etc.) and phrase-final intonation only.
new_statements.exceptions: None relating to stress. Tonal details: M-toned stems often reflect earlier *LH and LH flattens to M in allegro speech; noun-noun compound finals drop to L; dialectal variation in H-toned glottalic stems (Cv́ʔv́ in Bi/Ji vs Cv̄ʔv́ in Fl vs Cv̀ʔv́ in Ma).
new_statements.identity_note: The grammar describes Tiefo-D, the Tiefo variety of the Daramandugu village cluster (dialects Biton/Bi, Ji, Flaso/Fl, Masaso/Ma), which the authors state is a distinct language from Tiefo-N (Nyafogo and formerly Numudara; §1.2, p. 2). The catalog name "Tiefo-D" matches this variety; the work is not about Tiefo-N.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The record codes Tiefo-D as 'tonal' (no word stress) on the basis of Heath & Ouattara 2021, a 759-page open-access reference grammar that is the newest and most thorough description of the language and the top item in Glottolog's descriptive bibliography. I opened the text file we hold and confirmed all three deciding quotations verbatim at the cited printed pages (p.79 sec. 3.6, p.75 sec. 3.5, p.7 sec. 2.1.2), and confirmed the negative claim that the phonology chapter contains no stress section (TOC: 3.6 Tones, 3.7 Intonation; 'Metrically based vocalic processes' 3.4.1 is Heath's template heading covering apocope/epenthesis/schwa lenition and says nothing about prominence). Zenodo confirms no newer version of the grammar exists.
